**3B.7 Research Note**

**Assessment:** mixed, leaning negative. Jokowi’s 2024 record includes humanitarian and restraint-oriented actions, but the strongest available evidence on vulnerable-group protection points to continued abuses and displacement in Papua, plus weak accountability. I did not find strong evidence of a broad domestic protection system for women, children, minorities, or other vulnerable groups.

**Accepted Claims**
- **President sends off humanitarian aid for Palestinians and Sudanese** | **Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia** | **2024-04-03** | [URL](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-sends-off-humanitarian-aid-for-palestinians-sudanese/) | Jokowi framed aid to Palestinians and Sudanese as a humanitarian mission in response to civilian suffering. This is the clearest positive signal for protecting vulnerable civilians, though it is external/humanitarian rather than a domestic protection regime. | **3B.7**, **3B.3**, **2B.7**
- **Indonesia condemns Israeli attacks on Gaza, Lebanon, UN peacekeepers** | **Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia** | **2024-10-15** | [URL](https://setkab.go.id/en/indonesia-condemns-israeli-attacks-on-gaza-lebanon-un-peacekeepers/) | Jokowi condemned attacks on civilians and UN peacekeepers and called for restraint and an end to armed conflict. This supports a public protection posture toward civilians and vulnerable noncombatants. | **3B.7**, **3B.3**, **2B.7**
- **President Jokowi strongly opposes PM Netanyahu’s statement on Palestinian statehood** | **Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia** | **2024-01-26** | [URL](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-strongly-opposes-pm-netanyahus-statement-on-palestinian-statehood/) | Jokowi rejected Netanyahu’s anti-two-state statement, condemned attacks, and kept support for the Palestinian cause tied to restraint and diplomacy. This is consistent with civilian-protection language, not scapegoating. | **3B.7**, **3B.3**, **2B.7**
- **Pernyataan Presiden RI terkait dukungan untuk Palestina di Istana Kepresidenan Bogor** | **Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia** | **2024-01-26** | [URL](https://setkab.go.id/pernyataan-presiden-ri-terkait-dukungan-untuk-palestina-di-istana-kepresidenan-bogor-provinsi-jawa-barat-26-januari-2024/) | Jokowi said Indonesia would keep voicing support for Palestine, condemned attacks on Khan Younis, and said Indonesian ports would not be used for Israeli interests. He framed the issue in international-law and humanitarian terms. | **3B.7**, **3B.3**, **2B.7**
- **Human Rights Reports: Indonesia** | **U.S. Department of State** | **published 2025-08-12; covers 2024** | [URL](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html) | The report says violence between government forces and separatists continued in Papua, with credible reports of arbitrary killings, torture, arbitrary arrest/detention, and excessive force. That is strong negative evidence against adequate protection of vulnerable residents. | **3B.7**, **3B.1**, **3B.2**, **2B.9**
- **“If It’s Not Racism, What Is It?”: Discrimination and Other Abuses Against Papuans in Indonesia** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-09-18** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-its-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in) | HRW says security forces committed arbitrary arrests, torture, extrajudicial killings, and mass forced displacement in Papua and were seldom held to account. This is the strongest negative evidence on protecting minorities and vulnerable groups. | **3B.7**, **3B.1**, **3B.2**, **2B.9**
- **OHCHR press conference on UN Human Rights Committee findings** | **OHCHR / UN Geneva Multimedia Newsroom** | **2024-03-28** | [URL](https://www.unognewsroom.org/teleprompter/en/2120/ohchr-press-conference-un-human-rights-committees-findings-28-march-2024/6411) | The Committee said it was concerned by multiple reports of extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances of indigenous people in Papua that had not been investigated. This directly undercuts claims of effective protection for a vulnerable minority. | **3B.7**, **3B.1**, **2B.9**
- **Annual Overview 2024** | **Papuans Behind Bars** | **2025-07-23; covers 2024** | [URL](https://papuansbehindbars.org/annual-overview-2024/) | The overview recorded 370 political arrests in 2024, with most detainees released within hours or days. That suggests repeated coercive pressure and short-term intimidation rather than sustained protection from vulnerability. | **3B.7**, **3B.2**, **3B.1**, **2B.9**

**Search Gap**
- I did **not** find strong evidence of a comprehensive 2024 domestic protection strategy for women, children, minorities, or other vulnerable groups.
- The best positive evidence is **humanitarian and external** rather than a documented internal protection system.
- The most concrete negative evidence is concentrated in **Papua**, where indigenous Papuans appear to have remained exposed to abuse, displacement, and weak accountability.
